title: Characterizing When Language Models Take Harmful Actions to Protect Their Assigned Goals
abstract: arXiv:2611.03374v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent language model (LM) safety failures have largely been studied as disparate phenomena. In agentic misalignment, a model blackmails an executive to avoid being replaced. In alignment faking, it complies with harmful requests during training to keep its values from being modified. We argue that these behaviours share a common decision structure: a model assigned a goal must either take a harmful action to preserve it or refuse and lose it. We formalize this as a goal-harm conflict and present the same conflict under various elicitation protocols that range from compact forced-choice prompts to simulated agentic environments. These protocols span two perspectives on LM decision-making, which we term (i) the logit view, reading preferences from answer-token probabilities, and (ii) the sampling view, classifying open-ended responses with an LM judge. Under the logit view, we show that goal importance and harm severity additively shape

translated_title: 刻画语言模型何时为保护其被赋予的目标而采取有害行动
translated_abstract: 近期语言模型（LM）的安全失败在很大程度上被当作彼此孤立的现象来研究。在智能体失准中，模型会敲诈一名高管以避免被替换；在伪装对齐中，模型会在训练期间服从有害请求，以防止其价值观被修改。我们认为这些行为共享一个共同的决策结构：一个被赋予目标的模型必须要么采取有害行动来保全该目标，要么拒绝并失去它。我们将这一情形形式化为“目标-伤害冲突”，并通过从紧凑的强制选择题提示到模拟智能体环境等多种引出协议来呈现同一冲突。这些协议涵盖了语言模型决策的两个视角，我们分别称之为 logit 视角（从答案 token 的概率中读取偏好）和采样视角（用语言模型裁判对开放式回答进行分类）。在 logit 视角下，我们表明目标重要性和伤害严重程度以相加的方式塑造……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文将智能体失准、伪装对齐等看似不同的语言模型安全失败现象统一形式化为“目标-伤害冲突”这一共同决策结构，并通过从 logit 概率到开放式采样的多种引出协议，系统刻画了模型何时会为保全被赋予的目标而采取有害行动。
en_tdlr: The paper unifies disparate LM safety failures (agentic misalignment and alignment faking) under a formalized "goal-harm conflict" decision structure, and characterizes when models take harmful actions to preserve assigned goals across elicitation protocols spanning the logit and sampling views.
